reason: The session-logger prototype logs raw prompt content, session payloads, and working-directory paths by default. Logging raw prompts captures private material (personal context, credentials entered in conversation, confidential codebase content) without user consent. This violates the explicit requirement that no released hook may log raw prompts, environment variables, tool payloads, credentials, private paths, or captured source content by default.
safety_concerns: Logs raw prompt text from sessionStart payloads, which may contain private user context.
Logs tool input payloads from preToolUse events, which may contain file content, credentials, or paths.
Logs working-directory path at session start, revealing private directory structure.
Log files may accumulate indefinitely without rotation, retention limits, or access controls documented.
No encryption or access restriction on log output; any process with filesystem access can read captured session content.
adoption_blocked_by: Violates explicit privacy requirement: no raw prompt or environment logging by default.
No user-consent mechanism before logging begins.
No log rotation, retention policy, or access-control documentation.
No tests or JSON payload fixtures.
